beats.text: One ten-second kiss. Eighty million bacteria.
Researchers studied twenty-one couples. One partner drank a yogurt drink with traceable bacteria. Then they kissed for ten seconds.
Afterwards, those bacteria had tripled in the other partner's saliva. About eighty million swapped in one kiss.
Couples who kissed at least nine times a day had noticeably more similar saliva bacteria.
Oh, and the men said they kissed ten times a day. The women said five.
So yes, kissing literally makes you more alike. At least in your mouth.

sources: Kort, Caspers, van de Graaf, van Egmond, Keijser & Roeselers (2014). Shaping the oral microbiota through intimate kissing. Microbiome 2:41. 21 couples; probiotic tracer (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacteria) increased threefold in partner's saliva after a 10-s intimate kiss, est. 80 million bacteria; >= 9 intimate kisses/day associated with shared salivary microbiota; 74% of men reported kissing more often than partner (men 10/day, women 5/day). Via sci.news.
